title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-sophia-ramirez
content:
Account: Nebula Health (target)
Owner notes (quick): need to move this to an ILM email sequence + smaller TOFU assets for Product.

Background:
- Industry: digital health / clinical decision support
- Size: ~200 employees, Series B (recruiting ML/infra hires)
- HQ: Boston, US
- Tech signals: uses AWS, mentions TorchServe in recent blog; likely running models in-house for NER/clinical summarization; security docs -> HIPAA mention in investor deck
- Buying center (probable): CTO (Aman Shah), Head of ML (Leah Ortiz), VP Product (Marcus Lee), Security/Compliance (privacy lead)
- Current pain: latency at scale for batch+real-time summarization, high token cost, KV cache invalidation issues, slow model rollouts, audit/compliance constraints

Why Redwood might fit:
- Private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) + KMS/HSM integrations addresses HIPAA/data isolation concerns
- Dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput -> solves tail latency and bursty loads
- Optimize tooling (batching, quant recommendations) -> potential cost savings vs naive in-house hosting
- Rollouts + canary/A-B + tracing -> helps reduce risk of model regressions in production

Outbound outreach (first touch) - short subject lines & email drafts (A/B test):
Subject A: "Reduce inference costs for Nebula Health by 30% (quick ask)"
Subject B: "HIPAA-compliant LLM inference for clinical apps — 15 min?"

Email draft (short):
Hi Aman,

Quick one — I work on partnerships at Redwood Inference. We help teams running clinical LLM applications cut per-token costs and reduce tail latency while keeping data in VPCs or on-prem (HIPAA-friendly).

A few quick examples: dedicated GPU pools + automatic batching typically cuts unit cost 20–40% vs unmanaged endpoints, and our rollout/tracing tools reduce production regressions.

Would you be open to a 15-min intro next week to see if this aligns with your infra roadmap?

Thanks,
Sophia

LinkedIn touch (short):
Hi Aman — saw Nebula Health’s latest clinical summarization work. I lead partnerships at Redwood Inference — we help healthtech teams run LLM inference with HIPAA-safe private deployments and predictable latency. Quick chat?

Call agenda (if they accept):
- 5m intros / context
- 10m current infra + pain (latency, cost, compliance)
- 10m how Redwood maps to those (private, dedicated, optimize) + high-level pricing options
- 5m next steps / POC scope

Key objections + short rebuttals (prep):
1) "We already host models ourselves."
   - Rebuttal: totally makes sense. Two angles: 1) we often save teams money on unit cost (quantization + smarter batching + prefetching/KV cache) and free up infra ops time; 2) Redwood can run as private deployment in your VPC so you keep control + we add rollout/observability and SLOs. Offer a cost comparison POC: 2-week perf/cost baseline vs Redwood private.
2) "HIPAA / data privacy concerns."
   - Rebuttal: we support private control plane, customer-managed KMS/HSM, audit logs. Offer security whitepaper + SOC/ISO artifacts and set up an intro with our security team.
3) "Cost — we can’t justify another vendor."
   - Rebuttal: propose a focused POC on a high-volume endpoint to show unit-cost delta + latency improvements. Also call out reserved capacity pricing for predictable budgets.

Metrics to surface in POC / first deck:
- baseline tokens / month for target endpoint(s)
- current p50/p95/p99 latency
- current infra cost for inference (GPU hours, instance footprint)
- retention/compliance requirements (data residency, audit window)

Notes / research sources:
- Found Leah Ortiz on LinkedIn; commented on their July blog about "scaling clinical NER" — good entry point
- SEC filing for investor deck mentions "HIPAA-compliant data handling" (attach link in Confluence)
- G2 review mentions slow nightly batch jobs, potential to move to real-time

Next steps / action items:
- [ ] Send intro email A/B to Aman + Leah (target send: 2026-03-02)
- [ ] Create short 1-pager HIPAA + private deployment benefits (ask Solutions Eng for template)
- [ ] Book 15-min intro with Leah via LinkedIn (Priya to help)
- [ ] Open SFDC opp + add notes (SFDC-Account-001A7H000XYZ)
- [ ] Create POC scope doc (2-week cost & perf baseline) — tag: JIRA-7241

Meeting prep checklist:
- Bring examples of recent healthtech customers + anonymized cost deltas
- Security one-pager + SOC/ISO links ready
- Quick sketch of POC plan + what we need from them (sample traffic, model checkpoint, expected QPS)

Rough talk tracks / one-liners to try:
- "Many teams think inference cost is fixed; with smarter batching + quant recommendations we usually find 20–40% headroom."
- "You can keep keys & logs in your VPC — we plug into your KMS so data never leaves your control plane."

Random scratch ideas / experiments:
- Test a short outbound variant that leads with "HIPAA"
- Quick A/B: email that calls out a concrete % savings vs email that calls out "predictable latency SLA"

Misc: internal references
- Confluence notes: confluence://redwood/nebula-health-initial-research
- Jira: JIRA-7241 (POC scope)
- SFDC: SFDC-Account-001A7H000XYZ

-- Sophia

(Notes are rough — move to a cleaner playbook draft once we have a meeting)
